Equate the common ratios of consecutive terms in the geometric progression:
$$\frac{5k - 6}{3k} = \frac{6k - 4}{5k - 6}$$

Collect all terms on the left-hand side:
$$25k^2 - 18k^2 - 60k + 12k + 36 = 0 \implies 7k^2 - 48k + 36 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic equation in $k$:
$$7k^2 - 48k + 36 = 0 \implies (7k - 6)(k - 6) = 0$$
$$k = \frac{6}{7} \quad \text{or} \quad k = 6$$

Calculate the common ratio $r = \frac{5k - 6}{3k}$ for each value of $k$:
$$\text{For } k = \frac{6}{7}: \quad r = \frac{5\left(\frac{6}{7}\right) - 6}{3\left(\frac{6}{7}\right)} = \frac{\frac{30 - 42}{7}}{\frac{18}{7}} = -\frac{12}{18} = -\frac{2}{3}$$
$$\text{For } k = 6: \quad r = \frac{5(6) - 6}{3(6)} = \frac{30 - 6}{18} = \frac{24}{18} = \frac{4}{3}$$

The geometric progression converges when $|r| < 1$, which corresponds to $r = -\frac{2}{3}$ and $k = \frac{6}{7}$:
$$a = 3k = 3\left(\frac{6}{7}\right) = \frac{18}{7}$$

Calculate the sum to infinity:
$$S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{18}{7}}{1 - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)} = \frac{\frac{18}{7}}{\frac{5}{3}} = \frac{18}{7} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{54}{35} \quad (\approx 1.54)$$
